title: Section VIII. Of Liberty and Necessity
author: David Hume
summary: The dispute between liberty and necessity is merely verbal. All men have always believed in the regularity of human actions, which is all necessity amounts to, and liberty, properly understood as acting according to our will, is consistent with it and required by morality.

notes.on: the long disputed question concerning liberty and necessity
notes.note: Free will and determinism, in modern terms. Hume's claim that the two are compatible is an early statement of what is now called compatibilism.
Probably a transcription error for *government*; check against Selby-Bigge's text.
